correctness.rationale: For a pencil there is one singular point, so anti-admissibility is exactly independence of every meridian image from their total sum, plus surjectivity. In rank two over F_2, this forces the two allowed nonzero directions to occur with odd multiplicity, hence exactly even n; the converse assignment is explicit. For every odd prime a two-direction assignment with multiplicities 1 or 2 and n-r avoids both zero coefficients. For rank at least three, a basis assignment with all surplus meridians sent to e_1 leaves the total sum with nonzero e_2 and e_3 coordinates, proving all-prime anti-admissibility.

value.rationale: This is a complete classification for the most basic high-multiplicity incidence type omitted from the source's initial spectrum examples. It isolates exactly where characteristic two obstructs rank two, shows that rank three removes the obstruction for every odd pencil, and reveals a parity reversal relative to the neighboring near-pencil family. Because the source explicitly asks how multiplicity data controls smooth spectra, the pencil calculation is a natural benchmark rather than an arbitrary parameter slice.
